raw_response:
I’m 63 this year. Never went to school, can’t read the characters on the fertilizer bags, but I know my fields better than anyone with a diploma. I’ve been farming these plots since I was 28 — thirty-five years now. My son and his wife work over at the factory in town, so most days it’s just me and my old man in the fields. They only come back for the busy harvest times. We’ve got 8.5 mu total. Not much, but it feeds us and brings in a little cash.

I split it the same way I have for years: **5 mu for wheat then maize**, back to back, and **3.5 mu for sunflower**. I tried changing things once, about fifteen years ago, and lost money. Now I stick with what I know.

**Winter wheat** — I plant around the 8th of October, once the heat breaks. I save my own seed from last year, so I don’t pay for that. Before planting, I spread about one and a half bags of that compound fertilizer per mu — the shop man calls it something fancy, but I just ask for “the usual.” That’s what my neighbor Lao Zhang does too, and his wheat always looks fine. I irrigate three times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once when it greens up in spring, and once when the wheat is standing tall — I think they call it jointing. Pumping costs more every year, but if I skip it, the yield drops bad. I expect about 400 jin per mu, same as most years. Not great, not terrible.

**Summer maize** goes in the same 5 mu right after we cut the wheat, usually around June 12th or 15th. The window is tight — sometimes only five or six days. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, costs about 40 yuan per mu. My own saved maize seed doesn’t grow as good, learned that the hard way. I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. If the rains come nice, I irrigate once or twice in summer. Last year was too dry and I only got 400 jin per mu. I hope this year is wetter. I spray herbicide once, when the maize is small — the weeds would choke it otherwise.

**Sunflower** I plant on the other 3.5 mu, around late April when the soil warms up. I save my own sunflower seed. It’s hardy, doesn’t need much. I put down about half a bag of fertilizer per mu, just to give it a start. Irrigate once, maybe twice if it’s very dry. I expect 250 to 300 jin per mu. The oil press in town buys it, so it’s decent pocket money.

I don’t hire labor — can’t afford it. It’s all family. My old man and me do the planting and weeding. My son helps with harvest when he can get off work. Money is tight. Fertilizer prices went up again. I thought about buying less, but I’m scared of a bad yield. Better to spend a bit more and make sure we have enough to eat. We need cash for my granddaughter’s school fees too. So I’ll do what I did last year, maybe buy one less bag for the sunflower if I’m short. That’s the only place I can cut.
